composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Validate the body first so a missing or blank required field is a 400 before any
# owner is built or saved. It publishes the body for the build step to reuse.
validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  next: normalizeTelephone

# Strip non-digits from the telephone and require exactly 10 digits, so the owner is
# built and stored with the normalized value and a bad number is a 400.
normalizeTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  next: normalizeEmail

# The email is optional; when present it must be a valid address (else a 400) and is
# stored and returned lower-cased.
normalizeEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
  next: validatePostcode

# The postcode is optional; when present it must be 4 digits and valid for the city's
# region (else a 400), before any owner is built or saved. Stored and returned unchanged.
validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerPostcode
  next: ensureUniqueIdentity

# The single duplicate check: reject a request whose whole identity key (normalized
# telephone, email and household id) equals an existing owner's, as a 409, before any
# owner is built or saved. Because the telephone is part of the key, house-mates with
# different telephones have different keys and are both allowed.
ensureUniqueIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueIdentity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureCityCapacity

# Reject a request whose city already holds the maximum number of owners as a 409,
# before any owner is built or saved.
ensureCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: resolveRegistrationDate

# Resolve the effective registration date (supplied, else the server's current date) and
# roll a weekend forward to the next business day. Runs before the daily-limit check so
# the limit counts against the adjusted business day this create will land on.
resolveRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ResolveRegistrationDate
  next: ensureDailyLimit

# Reject a create once the maximum number of owners has already been registered on the
# resolved business day (by registrationDate) as a 429, before any owner is built or saved.
ensureDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: applyRegistrationDate

# Stamp the built owner with the resolved business-day registration date, overwriting any
# date the request body mapped in, so the owner is stored and returned with the adjusted day.
applyRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ApplyRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

# Assign the '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' customer code, where NNNN is one more than the current
# number of owners. Runs before save so the code is stored and returned with the owner.
assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignMembershipNumber

# Assign the '<customerCode>-M<YY>' membership number, where YY is the last two digits
# of the registration date year. Runs after the customer code and registration date are
# set and before save, so the number is stored and returned with the owner.
assignMembershipNumber:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignMembershipNumber
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# When the request opted in with 'sharesHousehold' and existing owners share this last
# name and address, assign the new owner and those members the same stable 'householdId'.
# Runs before save so the id is stored and returned with the owner.
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHouseholdSize

# Record the household's size after this create (members sharing the householdId plus the
# new owner), so the responder can promote a 3+ member household to the GOLD tier. Runs
# after the householdId is assigned and before save, so the size is stored with the owner.
assignHouseholdSize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdSize
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countNamesakes

# Record how many existing owners already share this owner's first and last name
# (case-insensitively). Runs before save so the count excludes the new owner and is
# stored and returned with it.
countNamesakes:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

# The save assigns the generated id, so audit here to log the created owner's id,
# customerCode and registrationDate to the AUDIT logger before responding.
audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

Read the whole pipeline (`owners.POST.yml`) and every function class it wires. Here is exactly what happens, in order, for `POST /api/owners`.

## Gate (whole endpoint)
- **Authorization** — `composition.authorize: hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')`. Without that role the request is denied (403 via the `AuthorizationDeniedException` handler) before any step runs.

## Pipeline steps (in `next:` order)

1. **`validate` — `ValidateOwnerFields`**
   - Binds the request body once (`@RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto`; note: no `@Valid` — validation is manual here).
   - *Side-effect:* normalizes `address` in place via `AddressNormalizer` (strip/collapse whitespace, upper-case, expand whole-word `ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`).
   - *Validation:* `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, `telephone` must be non-null/non-blank (address checked *after* normalization) → else `MissingOwnerFieldsException` (**400**).
   - *Side-effect:* republishes the DTO as a variable for later steps.

2. **`normalizeTelephone` — `NormalizeOwnerTelephone`**
   - *Validation + side-effect:* converts `telephone` to E.164 (`TelephoneNormalizer`: strips spaces/dashes/brackets; a leading `+` keeps its country code, otherwise assumes `+61` and drops one leading `0`; result must be `+` then 8–15 digits, and national length must match a known code — `+61`⇒9, `+1`⇒10). Invalid → `InvalidTelephoneException` (**400**). Valid value written back in place.

3. **`normalizeEmail` — `NormalizeOwnerEmail`**
   - Optional: null/blank left untouched.
   - *Validation:* if present must match the email regex → else `InvalidEmailException` (**400**).
   - *Side-effect:* stored trimmed + lower-cased.

4. **`validatePostcode` — `ValidateOwnerPostcode`**
   - Optional: null/blank left untouched.
   - *Validation:* if present must be exactly 4 digits, and (for a city with a known region) fall in that region's range → else `InvalidPostcodeException` (**400**). Value stored unchanged; unknown-region cities accept any 4-digit postcode.

5. **`ensureUniqueIdentity` — `EnsureUniqueIdentity`** *(transaction begins here; every step below is under `govern: [ transaction ]`)*
   - *Validation:* builds identity key `telephone|email|householdId` (household id resolved the same way `AssignHousehold` would) and rejects if it equals any existing owner's key → `DuplicateIdentityException` (**409**). This is the single duplicate check.

6. **`ensureCityCapacity` — `EnsureCityCapacity`**
   - *Validation:* if the owner's city (case-insensitive count) already holds ≥ 50 owners → `CityCapacityExceededException` (**409**).

7. **`resolveRegistrationDate` — `ResolveRegistrationDate`**
   - *Side-effect:* computes effective registration date = supplied date, else `LocalDate.now()`, then rolls a Saturday/Sunday forward to Monday (`BusinessDays`). Publishes it as a variable.

8. **`ensureDailyLimit` — `EnsureDailyLimit`**
   - *Validation:* if ≥ 100 owners already have that resolved registration date → `DailyLimitExceededException` (**429**).

9. **`build` — `BuildOwner`**
   - *Side-effect:* maps the DTO to an `Owner` entity (`OwnerMapper.toOwner`), publishes it.

10. **`applyRegistrationDate` — `ApplyRegistrationDate`**
    - *Side-effect:* stamps the resolved business-day date onto the owner, overwriting any date the body mapped in.

11. **`assignCustomerCode` — `AssignCustomerCode`**
    - *Side-effect:* sets `customerCode` = `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` (upper first-3 of city and last name; NNNN = current per-city owner count + 1, zero-padded).

12. **`assignMembershipNumber` — `AssignMembershipNumber`**
    - *Side-effect:* sets `membershipNumber` = `<customerCode>-M<YY>` (YY = last two digits of the registration-date year).

13. **`assignHousehold` — `AssignHousehold`**
    - Only when `sharesHousehold=true` **and** existing house-mates exist (same last name + normalized address).
    - *Side-effects:* sets the new owner's `householdId` to the stable SHA-256-derived id **and back-fills + saves** existing members that lack it (a write to *other* owner records). Otherwise leaves `householdId` unset.

14. **`assignHouseholdSize` — `AssignHouseholdSize`**
    - *Side-effect:* sets `householdSize` = (existing owners sharing the `householdId`) + 1 (so an owner with no household = 1).

15. **`countNamesakes` — `AssignNamesakeCount`**
    - *Side-effect:* sets `namesakeCount` = existing owners with the same first+last name (case-insensitive), excluding the not-yet-saved new owner.

16. **`save` — `SaveOwner`**
    - *Side-effect:* persists the owner; the generated id is assigned.

17. **`audit` — `AuditOwnerCreated`**
    - *Side-effect:* logs to the `AUDIT` logger: owner id, `customerCode`, `registrationDate`, and derived `membershipLevel` (`MembershipLevel.of`: base 1, +1 if email present, +1 if no namesakes, capped at 3).

18. **`respond` — `RespondWithOwnerCreated`**
    - *Side-effects:* maps to `OwnerDto`, sets the read-only `bulkSignupWarning` flag (true when > 80 owners registered on today's business day), and sends **201 Created** with `Location: /api/owners/{id}`.

## Notes
- Everything from step 5 onward runs inside one transaction (`govern: [ transaction ]`), so all persistence — the new owner plus any household back-fill saves — commits once at the end; any escalation before/within rolls back.
- Ordering is deliberate: field/format validations (400s) run before existence/capacity checks (409/429), and all rejections happen before `BuildOwner`, so nothing is built or saved for a request that will fail.
- `membershipLevel`, `bulkSignupWarning`, `householdSize`/GOLD-tier promotion, and the identity key are **derived** for the response/audit, not stored as validation gates.
